name: loka-wikidata-v10
notes: Same 44.5M-parameter BPE architecture as v6/v7/v8. Trained 20 epochs from random init on a 94,202-triple corpus extracted from a freshly-pulled 2,090,640-triple Loka slice (philippesaade/wikidata, 9,647 entity rows). Final epoch-20 perplexity 57.15 — best of any version, beating v8's 64.65 by 12% despite training on half the data. Two reasons coexisting: (a) the engine-wedge bug documented in paper §6.1 was fixed in commit 39effbb (single sled multi-tree transaction per /triples request instead of 3-4 per N-Triples line, no synchronous flush), unlocking sustained ingest at 500 triples/s without the 90k/174k/1M-triple wedge points; (b) the v9 corpus is preferentially the entities with closed reference graphs — when the HF stream doesn't provide an entity's row, its label-as-object dependencies drop the row at preprocess, leaving only the structurally well-connected core. v9 propgen test on the Q42 seed: 35 emissions, 34 of them on semantic predicates (97%) — best ratio yet. Residual failure mode is a URL-prefix shape leak on `Template:* | different from` predicates (analogous to v6's date-shape leak but in URL format, narrower predicate scope). See DEVLOG.md for the v6 -> v7 -> v8 -> v9 trajectory and paper §5.5 / §5.6 / §5.7.
